# Finding palette animations and dispatch table in game (2026-01-16 10:39Z)

_**User (2026-01-16 11:03Z)**_

now i want to find the code and the data for all palette animations in the game. We already know that room 0 and room 2 have both palette animations, one fade and the other rotate. I suspect room 9 has one as well for making certain objects shine. There must be a dispatch table for these. Find it and then all the associated data in the EXE. Document everything then rename on ghidra.

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nAnalyze the palette cycling dispatch table and configuration data in JUEGO.EXE\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\nprint(\"=\"*80)\nprint(\"PALETTE CYCLING SYSTEM ANALYSIS\")\nprint(\"=\"*80)\nprint()\n\n# Known config locations from documentation\nKNOWN_CONFIGS = {\n    2: 0x4B860,  # Room 2 (McDowells) - fade\n    0: 0x4B88C,  # Room 0 (City lights) - rotate\n}\n\n# First, scan the area around 0x4B800-0x4BA00 to find all 12-byte configs\nprint(\"Scanning for palette config structures...\")\nprint()\n\n# Scan for potential config patterns\n# Mode 1 = fade (single color), Mode 2-N = rotate (N colors)\n# Look for reasonable palette indices (0-255) followed by mode (1-10)\n\nconfigs_found = []\n\nfor offset in range(0x4B800, 0x4BA00):\n    if offset + 12 &gt; len(data):\n        continue\n    \n    palette_idx = data[offset]\n    mode = data[offset + 1]\n    \n    # Valid configs have mode 1-10 and palette index &lt; 256\n    if mode &gt;= 1 and mode &lt;= 10:\n        # For mode 1 (fade), check if RGB values are reasonable\n        if mode == 1:\n            current_r, current_g, current_b = data[offset+2], data[offset+3], data[offset+4]\n            min_r, min_g, min_b = data[offset+5], data[offset+6], data[offset+7]\n            max_r, max_g, max_b = data[offset+8], data[offset+9], data[offset+10]\n            flags = data[offset+11]\n            \n            # Check if RGB values are 6-bit (0-63) and make sense\n            if all(v &lt;= 63 for v in [current_r, current_g, current_b, min_r, min_g, min_b, max_r, max_g, max_b]):\n                if min_r &lt;= max_r and min_g &lt;= max_g and min_b &lt;= max_b:\n                    configs_found.append({\n                        'offset': offset,\n                        'mode': mode,\n                        'palette_idx': palette_idx,\n                        'raw': data[offset:offset+12]\n                    })\n        \n        # For mode &gt; 1 (rotate), look for delay value at offset +3\n        elif mode &gt;= 2:\n            # Byte 3 is typically delay (0-255)\n            delay = data[offset + 3]\n            if delay &gt; 0:\n                configs_found.append({\n                    'offset': offset,\n                    'mode': mode,\n                    'palette_idx': palette_idx,\n                    'raw': data[offset:offset+12]\n                })\n\n# De-duplicate (some configs may overlap detection)\nseen_offsets = set()\nunique_configs = []\nfor cfg in configs_found:\n    if cfg['offset'] not in seen_offsets:\n        seen_offsets.add(cfg['offset'])\n        unique_configs.append(cfg)\n\nprint(f\"Found {len(unique_configs)} potential configs:\")\nprint()\n\nfor cfg in unique_configs:\n    offset = cfg['offset']\n    raw = cfg['raw']\n    print(f\"File Offset: 0x{offset:08X}\")\n    print(f\"  Raw: {raw.hex(' ')}\")\n    print(f\"  Palette Index: {raw[0]} (0x{raw[0]:02X})\")\n    mode = raw[1]\n    print(f\"  Mode: {mode} ({'fade' if mode == 1 else f'rotate {mode} colors'})\")\n    \n    if mode == 1:\n        print(f\"  Current RGB: ({raw[2]}, {raw[3]}, {raw[4]}) = 8-bit: ({raw[2]*4}, {raw[3]*4}, {raw[4]*4})\")\n        print(f\"  Min RGB:     ({raw[5]}, {raw[6]}, {raw[7]}) = 8-bit: ({raw[5]*4}, {raw[6]*4}, {raw[7]*4})\")\n        print(f\"  Max RGB:     ({raw[8]}, {raw[9]}, {raw[10]}) = 8-bit: ({raw[8]*4}, {raw[9]*4}, {raw[10]*4})\")\n        print(f\"  Flags: 0x{raw[11]:02X}\")\n    else:\n        print(f\"  Delay: {raw[3]} frames\")\n        print(f\"  Other bytes: {raw[2:].hex(' ')}\")\n    print()\n\n# Now search for the dispatch table\nprint(\"=\"*80)\nprint(\"DISPATCH TABLE SEARCH\")\nprint(\"=\"*80)\nprint()\n\n# The dispatch table at memory 0x486a4 contains 6-byte entries:\n# - bytes 0-1: room number (word)\n# - bytes 2-5: pointer to config (dword)\n# Terminated by 0xFFFF\n\n# Calculate approximate file offset\n# Memory 0x486a4 -&gt; file offset should be around 0x4B6A4 based on known mapping\n\n# Search for the table by looking for sequences ending in FF FF\nfor start in range(0x4B600, 0x4B800):\n    # Try to parse as table entries\n    entries = []\n    pos = start\n    valid = True\n    \n    while pos &lt; len(data) - 2:\n        room = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[pos:pos+2])[0]\n        if room == 0xFFFF:\n            break\n        if room &gt; 60:  # More than 60 rooms is suspicious\n            valid = False\n            break\n        if pos + 6 &gt; len(data):\n            valid = False\n            break\n        ptr = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[pos+2:pos+6])[0]\n        entries.append((room, ptr))\n        pos += 6\n    \n    # Check if we found a valid table\n    if valid and len(entries) &gt;= 2 and data[pos:pos+2] == b'\\xff\\xff':\n        # Verify entries point to reasonable config addresses\n        has_valid_ptrs = True\n        for room, ptr in entries:\n            # Pointers should be in memory range for data segment\n            if ptr &lt; 0x40000 or ptr &gt; 0x60000:\n                has_valid_ptrs = False\n                break\n        \n        if has_valid_ptrs:\n            print(f\"Found dispatch table at file offset 0x{start:08X}\")\n            print(f\"Terminator at 0x{pos:08X}\")\n            print(f\"Memory address would be ~0x{start - 0x3000:08X}\")\n            print()\n            print(\"Entries:\")\n            for room, ptr in entries:\n                # Convert memory pointer to file offset (approximate)\n                file_ptr = ptr + 0x3000  # Adjust based on segment mapping\n                print(f\"  Room {room:2d}: config pointer = 0x{ptr:08X} (file ~0x{file_ptr:08X})\")\n            print()\n\n# Direct scan of documented table location\nprint(\"=\"*80)\nprint(\"DIRECT TABLE READ AT DOCUMENTED LOCATION\")\nprint(\"=\"*80)\nprint()\n\n# Based on existing docs, the table is around 0x4B6A4 in file\ntable_start = 0x4B6A4\nprint(f\"Reading at file offset 0x{table_start:08X}:\")\nprint()\n\npos = table_start\nentries = []\nwhile pos &lt; len(data) - 2:\n    room = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[pos:pos+2])[0]\n    if room == 0xFFFF:\n        print(f\"  0x{pos:08X}: TERMINATOR (0xFFFF)\")\n        break\n    ptr = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[pos+2:pos+6])[0]\n    entries.append((room, ptr, pos))\n    print(f\"  0x{pos:08X}: Room {room:2d} -&gt; config at memory 0x{ptr:08X}\")\n    pos += 6\n\nprint()\nprint(\"Config data for each entry:\")\nprint()\n\nfor room, mem_ptr, table_pos in entries:\n    # Convert memory address to file offset\n    # Based on known configs: mem 0x4B860 is documented for room 2\n    # We need to find the segment base\n    \n    # Try different segment mappings\n    for seg_offset in [0x0, 0x3000, 0x2F00, 0x3100]:\n        file_ptr = mem_ptr + seg_offset\n        if 0x4B800 &lt;= file_ptr &lt;= 0x4B900:\n            if file_ptr + 12 &lt;= len(data):\n                raw = data[file_ptr:file_ptr+12]\n                print(f\"Room {room}: file offset 0x{file_ptr:08X}\")\n                print(f\"  Raw bytes: {raw.hex(' ')}\")\n                mode = raw[1]\n                print(f\"  Palette idx: {raw[0]}, Mode: {mode}\")\n                print()\n                break\n",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nComplete Palette Cycling System Analysis for Alfred Pelrock\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\nprint(\"=\"*80)\nprint(\"ALFRED PELROCK - PALETTE CYCLING DISPATCH TABLE ANALYSIS\")\nprint(\"=\"*80)\nprint()\n\n# The dispatch table starts at file offset 0x4B830 based on analysis\n# Format: 6-byte entries with terminator 0xFFFF\n# Bytes 0-1: room number (word, little-endian)\n# Bytes 2-5: offset to 12-byte config (dword, little-endian) - RELATIVE to table start or segment\n\nTABLE_START = 0x4B830\nTERMINATOR = 0xFFFF\n\n# First, find a reliable mapping\n# We know Room 0 config is at 0x4B88C and Room 2 config is at 0x4B860\n\n# Read the table\nprint(f\"Dispatch Table at file offset 0x{TABLE_START:08X}:\")\nprint()\n\npos = TABLE_START\nentries = []\nwhile pos + 2 &lt;= len(data):\n    room = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[pos:pos+2])[0]\n    if room == TERMINATOR:\n        print(f\"  0x{pos:08X}: TERMINATOR (0xFFFF)\")\n        break\n    if pos + 6 &gt; len(data):\n        break\n    offset = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[pos+2:pos+6])[0]\n    entries.append({\n        'room': room,\n        'table_offset': pos,\n        'config_offset_raw': offset\n    })\n    print(f\"  0x{pos:08X}: Room {room:2d} -&gt; offset 0x{offset:08X}\")\n    pos += 6\n\nprint()\nprint(f\"Total entries: {len(entries)}\")\nprint()\n\n# Now figure out the offset calculation\n# Looking at the raw offsets vs known config locations:\n# - Room 2 config at 0x4B860\n# - Room 0 config at 0x4B88C\n# The offsets in the table should point to these\n\nprint(\"=\"*80)\nprint(\"OFFSET MAPPING ANALYSIS\")\nprint(\"=\"*80)\nprint()\n\n# Find room 0 and room 2 entries\nfor entry in entries:\n    if entry['room'] == 0:\n        print(f\"Room 0 entry: raw offset = 0x{entry['config_offset_raw']:08X}\")\n        # Known file offset is 0x4B88C\n        # If raw offset is segment-relative, we need to find the base\n        diff = 0x4B88C - entry['config_offset_raw']\n        print(f\"  Known config at file 0x4B88C, difference = 0x{diff:08X}\")\n    if entry['room'] == 2:\n        print(f\"Room 2 entry: raw offset = 0x{entry['config_offset_raw']:08X}\")\n        # Known file offset is 0x4B860\n        diff = 0x4B860 - entry['config_offset_raw']\n        print(f\"  Known config at file 0x4B860, difference = 0x{diff:08X}\")\n\nprint()\n\n# The offsets appear to be memory addresses in the data segment\n# Let's compute a base: segment starts at 0x40000 in memory = file offset X\n# If room 0 offset is 0x4B88C relative to file start, memory offset would be...\n\n# Actually let's look at what addresses would make sense\n# From load_room_and_init_alfred, table is at &amp;DAT_000486a4\n# In memory address 0x000486a4\n\n# Memory to file mapping for data segment:\n# Memory 0x486a4 -&gt; File 0x4B830 (difference = 0x318C)\n# So config memory 0x4B88C would be file 0x4B88C (it's stored as file offsets directly!)\n\nprint(\"=\"*80)\nprint(\"PALETTE CONFIG STRUCTURES\")\nprint(\"=\"*80)\nprint()\n\n# The offsets in the table are MEMORY addresses in the data segment\n# Memory address to file offset: subtract 0x318C (approximately)\n# Or they might be direct file offsets if stored as absolute file positions\n\n# Let's try interpreting them as direct file offsets\nfor entry in entries:\n    room = entry['room']\n    raw_offset = entry['config_offset_raw']\n    \n    # Try different interpretations\n    # 1. Direct file offset\n    if 0x4B800 &lt;= raw_offset &lt;= 0x4BA00:\n        file_offset = raw_offset\n    else:\n        # 2. Memory address - convert to file offset\n        # Memory base ~= 0x40000, file base varies\n        # From table: memory 0x486a4 = file 0x4B830\n        # Diff = 0x318C\n        file_offset = raw_offset + 0x318C\n    \n    # Try to read config at calculated offset\n    if 0 &lt; file_offset &lt; len(data) - 12:\n        config = data[file_offset:file_offset+12]\n        palette_idx = config[0]\n        mode = config[1]\n        \n        # Validate - mode should be 1-10, palette idx should be &lt; 256\n        if mode &gt;= 1 and mode &lt;= 10:\n            print(f\"Room {room:2d}: File offset 0x{file_offset:08X}\")\n            print(f\"  Raw bytes: {config.hex(' ')}\")\n            print(f\"  Palette index: {palette_idx} (0x{palette_idx:02X})\")\n            \n            if mode == 1:\n                # Fade mode\n                current = (config[2], config[3], config[4])\n                min_rgb = (config[5], config[6], config[7])\n                max_rgb = (config[8], config[9], config[10])\n                flags = config[11]\n                print(f\"  Mode: FADE (1)\")\n                print(f\"  Current RGB (6-bit): {current} -&gt; 8-bit: ({current[0]*4}, {current[1]*4}, {current[2]*4})\")\n                print(f\"  Min RGB (6-bit): {min_rgb} -&gt; 8-bit: ({min_rgb[0]*4}, {min_rgb[1]*4}, {min_rgb[2]*4})\")\n                print(f\"  Max RGB (6-bit): {max_rgb} -&gt; 8-bit: ({max_rgb[0]*4}, {max_rgb[1]*4}, {max_rgb[2]*4})\")\n                print(f\"  Flags: 0x{flags:02X}\")\n                print(f\"    Speed: {flags &amp; 0x3F}\")\n                print(f\"    Direction: {'down' if flags &amp; 0x40 else 'up'}\")\n            else:\n                # Rotate mode\n                delay = config[3]\n                print(f\"  Mode: ROTATE ({mode} colors)\")\n                print(f\"  Delay: {delay} frames (~{delay/18:.1f} seconds at 18 FPS)\")\n                print(f\"  Other bytes: {config[2:].hex(' ')}\")\n            print()\n",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nComplete Palette Cycling Dispatch Table Analysis for Alfred Pelrock\n\nMemory address 0x486a4 contains the dispatch table for palette cycling.\nThis script maps memory addresses to file offsets and extracts all config data.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\nprint(\"=\"*80)\nprint(\"ALFRED PELROCK - COMPLETE PALETTE CYCLING ANALYSIS\")\nprint(\"=\"*80)\nprint()\n\n# The EXE file layout:\n# DOS MZ header is 0x200 bytes typically\n# Segments are loaded at various addresses\n\n# From Ghidra, we know:\n# - Memory address 0x486a4 = dispatch table\n# - The code reads 6-byte entries: word room_num, dword config_ptr\n# - Terminated by 0xFFFF\n\n# We need to find the memory-to-file offset mapping.\n# Let's search for the table by looking for the terminator pattern\n\n# Known config data locations (from documentation):\n# Room 2: file 0x4B860, bytes: fa 01 24 2c 08 0c 14 08 24 2c 08 05\n# Room 0: file 0x4B88C, bytes: c8 06 00 5a e0 04 00 04 67 07 00 01\n\n# Search for these patterns to verify file offsets\nprint(\"Verifying known config locations...\")\nroom2_pattern = bytes.fromhex('fa 01 24 2c 08 0c 14 08 24 2c 08 05')\nroom0_pattern = bytes.fromhex('c8 06 00 5a e0 04 00 04 67 07 00 01')\n\nroom2_file_offset = data.find(room2_pattern)\nroom0_file_offset = data.find(room0_pattern)\n\nprint(f\"Room 2 config at file offset: 0x{room2_file_offset:08X}\")\nprint(f\"Room 0 config at file offset: 0x{room0_file_offset:08X}\")\nprint()\n\n# Now search for a dispatch table that contains entries pointing to these configs\n# The table format is: [room_num:2][config_ptr:4] * N + [0xFFFF:2]\n\n# The config_ptr values in the table are MEMORY addresses\n# We need to figure out: file_offset = memory_address + DELTA\n# If room 2 config is at file 0x4B860 and memory ptr is X, then DELTA = 0x4B860 - X\n\n# Let's scan for potential table locations\nprint(\"Searching for dispatch table...\")\nprint()\n\n# Look for a table with entries for rooms 0, 2, 9, etc.\n# Table should have room numbers &lt; 60 and terminate with 0xFFFF\n\nfor table_start in range(0x48000, 0x4C000):\n    entries = []\n    pos = table_start\n    valid = True\n    \n    while pos + 6 &lt;= len(data):\n        room = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[pos:pos+2])[0]\n        if room == 0xFFFF:\n            # Found terminator\n            break\n        if room &gt; 60:\n            valid = False\n            break\n        ptr = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[pos+2:pos+6])[0]\n        entries.append((room, ptr, pos))\n        pos += 6\n        \n        if len(entries) &gt; 20:  # Safety limit\n            valid = False\n            break\n    \n    # Check if this looks like a valid table\n    if valid and len(entries) &gt;= 2 and pos + 2 &lt;= len(data) and data[pos:pos+2] == b'\\xff\\xff':\n        # Check if entries include room 0 or room 2\n        rooms_found = set(e[0] for e in entries)\n        if 0 in rooms_found or 2 in rooms_found:\n            print(f\"Potential table at file offset 0x{table_start:08X}\")\n            print(f\"  {len(entries)} entries, terminator at 0x{pos:08X}\")\n            \n            # For each entry, try to compute the delta\n            for room, ptr, entry_pos in entries:\n                print(f\"  Entry at 0x{entry_pos:08X}: Room {room:2d}, memory ptr 0x{ptr:08X}\")\n            \n            # If we have room 0 or room 2, compute delta\n            for room, ptr, _ in entries:\n                if room == 0 and room0_file_offset &gt;= 0:\n                    delta = room0_file_offset - ptr\n                    print(f\"\\n  DELTA computation (room 0): file 0x{room0_file_offset:08X} - mem 0x{ptr:08X} = 0x{delta:08X}\")\n                if room == 2 and room2_file_offset &gt;= 0:\n                    delta = room2_file_offset - ptr\n                    print(f\"  DELTA computation (room 2): file 0x{room2_file_offset:08X} - mem 0x{ptr:08X} = 0x{delta:08X}\")\n            print()\n            print(\"=\"*60)\n            print()\n\n# Now let's try a different approach - search for the table by pattern matching\n# The table should have entries like: 00 00 XX XX XX XX 02 00 YY YY YY YY FF FF\nprint(\"Alternative search: looking for (room 0 entry, room 2 entry) pattern...\")\n\nfor i in range(0x48000, 0x4C000):\n    # Look for two consecutive entries for rooms 0 and 2 or 2 and 0\n    if i + 14 &gt; len(data):\n        continue\n    \n    room1 = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[i:i+2])[0]\n    room2_check = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[i+6:i+8])[0]\n    \n    if (room1 == 0 and room2_check == 2) or (room1 == 2 and room2_check == 0):\n        ptr1 = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[i+2:i+6])[0]\n        ptr2 = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[i+8:i+12])[0]\n        \n        print(f\"Found at 0x{i:08X}:\")\n        print(f\"  Room {room1}: ptr 0x{ptr1:08X}\")\n        print(f\"  Room {room2_check}: ptr 0x{ptr2:08X}\")\n        \n        # Check for terminator nearby\n        for j in range(i + 12, min(i + 100, len(data) - 2)):\n            if data[j:j+2] == b'\\xff\\xff':\n                print(f\"  Terminator at 0x{j:08X}\")\n                break\n        print()\n",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\nimport struct\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\nprint(\"Raw hex dump of palette config region (0x4B860 - 0x4B8F4):\")\nprint()\nstart = 0x4B860\nfor i in range(start, 0x4B8F4, 16):\n    hex_str = data[i:i+16].hex(' ')\n    print(f\"0x{i:08X}: {hex_str}\")\n\nprint()\nprint(\"=\"*80)\nprint(\"Config entries at 4-byte boundaries (configs seem to be 4 bytes apart!):\")\nprint()\n\n# The dispatch table points to configs at 4-byte intervals, not 12-byte\n# Let's verify by checking the pointers:\n# Room 2: 0x8660\n# Room 9: 0x8674 (diff: 0x14 = 20 bytes)\n# Room 17: 0x866C (diff from room 2: 0xC = 12 bytes)\n# Room 18: 0x8670 (diff: 4 bytes)\n# etc.\n\n# So configs are NOT sequential - they're stored compactly and pointers\n# are adjusted for each room\n\n# Let's see all the unique config locations\nconfigs = {}\npos = 0x4B8A4\nDATA_BASE = 0x43200\n\nwhile True:\n    room = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[pos:pos+2])[0]\n    if room == 0xFFFF:\n        break\n    ptr = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[pos+2:pos+6])[0]\n    file_offset = ptr + DATA_BASE\n    configs[room] = file_offset\n    pos += 6\n\nprint(\"All config locations sorted by file offset:\")\nfor room, offset in sorted(configs.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]):\n    print(f\"  0x{offset:08X}: Room {room:2d}\")\n\n# Let's see the actual memory layout - configs share some bytes\nprint()\nprint(\"=\"*80)\nprint(\"Config data with proper parsing:\")\nprint()\n\nfor room in sorted(configs.keys()):\n    offset = configs[room]\n    config = data[offset:offset+12]\n    print(f\"Room {room:2d} at 0x{offset:08X}: {config.hex(' ')}\")\n    \n    palette_idx = config[0]\n    mode = config[1]\n    if mode == 1:\n        print(f\"  FADE: palette {palette_idx}, min=({config[5]},{config[6]},{config[7]}), max=({config[8]},{config[9]},{config[10]})\")\n    else:\n        print(f\"  ROTATE: palette {palette_idx}, {mode} colors, delay={config[3]} frames\")\n    print()\n",

  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "# Palette Cycling/Animation System Documentation\n\n## Overview\n\nAlfred Pelrock uses a palette cycling system to create animated visual effects without modifying pixel data. The game modifies VGA palette entries in real-time to create effects like:\n\n- Fading neon signs (McDowells restaurant)\n- Rotating/shimmering lights (city windows at night)  \n- Shiny/glowing objects (gems, buttons)\n- Water/fire effects\n\nThis technique was common in DOS-era games as it's extremely efficient - only 3 bytes per color need to change rather than thousands of pixels.\n\n## Data Structures\n\n### Dispatch Table\n\n**Location:**\n- Memory address: &#96;0x000486A4&#96;\n- File offset: &#96;0x0004B8A4&#96;\n- Ghidra label: &#96;palette_cycling_dispatch_table&#96;\n\n**Format:** Array of 6-byte entries terminated by &#96;0xFFFF&#96;\n\n| Offset | Size | Field | Description |\n|--------|------|-------|-------------|\n| +0 | 2 | room_number | Room ID (little-endian word) |\n| +2 | 4 | config_ptr | Pointer to 12-byte config structure |\n\n**Terminator:** &#96;0xFFFF&#96; marks end of table\n\n### Config Structure (12 bytes)\n\nTwo modes exist: FADE (mode=1) and ROTATE (mode&gt;1)\n\n#### FADE Mode (mode=1)\nSmoothly transitions a single palette entry between two colors.\n\n| Offset | Size | Field | Description |\n|--------|------|-------|-------------|\n| +0 | 1 | palette_index | VGA palette entry to animate (0-255) |\n| +1 | 1 | mode | Always 1 for fade |\n| +2 | 1 | current_r | Current red value (6-bit, 0-63) |\n| +3 | 1 | current_g | Current green value (6-bit, 0-63) |\n| +4 | 1 | current_b | Current blue value (6-bit, 0-63) |\n| +5 | 1 | min_r | Minimum red value |\n| +6 | 1 | min_g | Minimum green value |\n| +7 | 1 | min_b | Minimum blue value |\n| +8 | 1 | max_r | Maximum red value |\n| +9 | 1 | max_g | Maximum green value |\n| +10 | 1 | max_b | Maximum blue value |\n| +11 | 1 | flags | Control flags (see below) |\n\n**Flags byte:**\n- Bits 0-5: Speed (steps per frame)\n- Bit 6: Direction (0=fading toward min, 1=fading toward max)\n\n#### ROTATE Mode (mode&gt;1)\nCyclically rotates N consecutive palette entries.\n\n| Offset | Size | Field | Description |\n|--------|------|-------|-------------|\n| +0 | 1 | start_index | First palette entry to rotate |\n| +1 | 1 | count | Number of consecutive entries (2-10) |\n| +2 | 1 | reserved | Usually 0 |\n| +3 | 1 | delay | Frames between rotations |\n| +4-11 | 8 | state_data | Runtime state/reserved |\n\n## Rooms with Palette Animation\n\n| Room | Mode | Palette Range | Delay | Effect Description |\n|------|------|---------------|-------|-------------------|\n| 0 | ROTATE-6 | 200-205 | 90 frames (~5 sec) | City window lights at night |\n| 2 | FADE | 250 | - | McDowells neon sign (green glow) |\n| 9 | ROTATE-4 | 252-255 | 4 frames | Shiny object effect |\n| 17 | ROTATE-6 | 138-143 | 8 frames | Unknown |\n| 18 | ROTATE-6 | 181-186 | 35 frames | Unknown |\n| 19 | FADE | 37 | - | Red glow effect |\n| 21 | ROTATE-3 | 148-150 | 10 frames | Unknown |\n| 25 | ROTATE-4 | 224-227 | 4 frames | Unknown |\n| 32 | ROTATE-2 | 203-204 | 2 frames | Unknown |\n| 33 | ROTATE-2 | 214-215 | 2 frames | Unknown |\n| 38 | ROTATE-7 | 103-109 | 1 frame | Fast shimmer |\n| 39 | ROTATE-3 | 192-194 | 5 frames | Unknown |\n| 46 | ROTATE-2 | 43-44 | 4 frames | Unknown |\n\n## File Offsets\n\n### Dispatch Table\n- **File offset:** &#96;0x0004B8A4&#96;\n- **Size:** 80 bytes (13 entries × 6 bytes + 2 byte terminator)\n\n### Config Data Block\n- **File offset:** &#96;0x0004B860&#96; to &#96;0x0004B8A3&#96;\n- **Size:** 68 bytes\n- **Note:** Configs overlap to save space - each room's 12-byte config shares bytes with adjacent configs\n\n### Individual Config Offsets\n\n| Room | File Offset | Memory Ptr |\n|------|-------------|------------|\n| 2 | 0x0004B860 | 0x00008660 |\n| 17 | 0x0004B86C | 0x0000866C |\n| 18 | 0x0004B870 | 0x00008670 |\n| 9 | 0x0004B874 | 0x00008674 |\n| 19 | 0x0004B878 | 0x00008678 |\n| 21 | 0x0004B884 | 0x00008684 |\n| 39 | 0x0004B888 | 0x00008688 |\n| 0 | 0x0004B88C | 0x0000868C |\n| 25 | 0x0004B890 | 0x00008690 |\n| 38 | 0x0004B894 | 0x00008694 |\n| 32 | 0x0004B898 | 0x00008698 |\n| 33 | 0x0004B89C | 0x0000869C |\n| 46 | 0x0004B8A0 | 0x000086A0 |\n\n## Code References\n\n### Main ## Summary

I've fully analyzed and documented the palette animation system in Alfred Pelrock. Here's what was discovered:

### Dispatch Table
- **Location:** File offset `0x4B8A4`, Memory address `0x486A4`
- **Format:** 6-byte entries (room:2 + config_ptr:4), terminated by `0xFFFF`
- **13 rooms** have palette animations

### Rooms with Palette Animation

| Room | Mode | Effect |
|------|------|--------|
| **0** | ROTATE-6 | City window lights (palette 200-205, 90 frame delay) |
| **2** | FADE | McDowells neon sign green glow (palette 250) |
| **9** | ROTATE-4 | Shiny/shimmering effect (palette 252-255, fast 4 frame delay) |
| **17** | ROTATE-6 | Unknown (palette 138-143) |
| **18** | ROTATE-6 | Unknown (palette 181-186) |
| **19** | FADE | Red glow effect (palette 37) |
| **21** | ROTATE-3 | Unknown (palette 148-150) |
| **25** | ROTATE-4 | Unknown (palette 224-227) |
| **32** | ROTATE-2 | Unknown (palette 203-204) |
| **33** | ROTATE-2 | Unknown (palette 214-215) |
| **38** | ROTATE-7 | Fast shimmer (palette 103-109, 1 frame delay!) |
| **39** | ROTATE-3 | Unknown (palette 192-194) |
| **46** | ROTATE-2 | Unknown (palette 43-44) |

### Ghidra Renames Applied
- `palette_cycling_dispatch_table` @ 0x486A4
- `palette_cycling_enabled` @ 0x4F8EA
- `palette_cycling_config_ptr` @ 0x4F8EC
- `palette_cycling_frame_counter` @ 0x51753
- `current_room_palette_ptr` @ 0x4FAB8
- `outport_byte` (renamed from FUN_0002b11b)
- Added decompiler comments explaining the system

### Documentation
Created `PALETTE_ANIMATION_SYSTEM.md` with:
- Complete structure documentation
- All file/memory offsets
- Raw hex dumps
- Algorithm pseudocode
- Memory-to-file mapping formula: `file_offset = memory_ptr + 0x43200`

Room 9 is missing a `break;` statement, so it falls through to room 17's offset. This means room 9 is loading room 17's palette animation config instead of its own.

Let me verify what room 17's config is: Good, I can see the documentation confirms:
- Room 9: ROTATE-4, palette 252-255, 4 frames delay
- Room 17: ROTATE-6, palette 138-143, 8 frames delay

So the bug is clear - room 9's case is falling through to room 17's offset (0x4B86C), which loads palette starting at index 138 (which is probably carpet colors) instead of 252 (the Egyptian logo).

**The fix is simple:** Add a `break;` after the room 9 case. Fixed! The bug was a **missing `break;` statement** in the switch case for room 9. 

Without the break, room 9 fell through to room 17's case, so it was loading:
- Room 17's config offset `0x4B86C` → palette index **138** (carpet colors)

Instead of:
- Room 9's config offset `0x4B874` → palette index **252** (Egyptian logo)

This is a classic C/C++ switch fall-through bug. Now room 9 will properly animate palette entries 252-255 (the Egyptian logo on the desk) with the ROTATE-4 effect at 4 frames delay.

  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Check palette index 37 in room 19\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\n# Read room 19 data from ALFRED.1\nwith open('/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/files/ALFRED.1', 'rb') as f:\n    # Read room directory (56 rooms * 13 pairs * 8 bytes = 5824 bytes)\n    f.seek(19 * 13 * 8)  # Room 19, pair 0\n    pair0_offset, pair0_size = struct.unpack('&lt;II', f.read(8))\n    \n    # Read pair 11 for palette\n    f.seek(19 * 13 * 8 + 11 * 8)\n    palette_offset, palette_size = struct.unpack('&lt;II', f.read(8))\n    \n    # Read palette\n    f.seek(palette_offset)\n    palette_data = f.read(768)  # 256 colors * 3 bytes\n    \n    # Read background (pair 0)\n    f.seek(pair0_offset)\n    bg_data = f.read(pair0_size)\n\n# Parse palette\npalette = []\nfor i in range(256):\n    r = palette_data[i*3]\n    g = palette_data[i*3+1]\n    b = palette_data[i*3+2]\n    palette.append((r, g, b))\n\nout = []\nout.append(f\"Room 19 Palette Index 37:\")\nout.append(f\"  RGB (6-bit VGA): {palette[37]}\")\nout.append(f\"  RGB (8-bit): ({palette[37][0]&lt;&lt;2}, {palette[37][1]&lt;&lt;2}, {palette[37][2]&lt;&lt;2})\")\n\n# Count pixels using index 37\ncount = 0\nfor b in bg_data[:320*200]:  # First 64000 bytes = raw image data\n    if b == 37:\n        count += 1\n\nout.append(f\"  Pixels using index 37: {count}\")\n\n# Show surrounding palette entries\nout.append(\"\")\nout.append(\"Nearby palette entries for context:\")\nfor idx in range(35, 45):\n    r, g, b = palette[idx]\n    out.append(f\"  Index {idx}: RGB({r}, {g}, {b}) = ({r&lt;&lt;2}, {g&lt;&lt;2}, {b&lt;&lt;2}) 8-bit\")\n\n# Output to file\nwith open('/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/room19_palette_check.txt', 'w') as f:\n    f.write('\\n'.join(out))\n\nprint(\"Done - check room19_palette_check.txt\")\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}
